task: Bring the three static Chat banner customer-config components (bannerMessage, bannerLinkLabel, bannerLinkRoute) into the EPMCDME-13983 dynamic customer configuration mechanism as one logical Administration item, with the static YAML values as fallback and dynamic values overriding them without redeploy.

key_reasoning.reason: Six components across two repositories: BE declaration registry (customer_config_declarations.py), BE merge/resolution layer (customer_config_service.py), customer-config.yaml, FE Banner.tsx, FE appInfo store getters, FE configKeys.ts. The fallback logic lands inside the shared resolve/merge path that also serves chatDisclaimer, /v1/config and /v1/applications, so AC-8 (disclaimer unaffected) is a live regression surface rather than a given.

Acceptance criteria are detailed, but AC-2 (one logical item) structurally conflicts with AC-3/AC-4 (three static ids as fallback): SettingDeclaration is hard-wired one-to-one with a component_id. Three open decisions must be made before implementation — grouped id vs extended declaration model, the precedence rule for reading legacy ids as defaults (the externally-managed ConfigMap cannot be seeded from this repo), which enabled flag governs a grouped item, and the localStorage dismissal key that hashes bannerMessage (an observable behaviour change sitting against AC-7).

The declaration-append pattern is established and rollback is trivial (delete a dynamic_config row, no migration), but the legacy-id fallback is genuinely new merge logic that 13983 does not provide. Security weight: bannerLinkRoute flows unvalidated into a react-router Link and /v1/config is unauthenticated, so it needs a pattern/pattern_message plus BE validation — note Markup.PLAIN does not run the link-scheme sanitiser.

Roughly 8-12 files across two repos and 5+ directories: 2-4 backend source files plus 2-3 test files (declarations, service merge, and the currently absent router-level tests the BE testing guide requires), and 3-5 frontend files including a rewrite of Banner.test.tsx (which mocks the three getters directly) and a new reactivity integration test modelled on ChatDisclaimer.integration.test.tsx.

Four distinct layers — FE UI/store, BE API payload shape, BE service/merge, BE config plus dynamic_config persistence — and the change is cross-repo with merge-order coupling (FE-first yields an empty banner, BE-first yields an admin card editing a value nothing consumes). No alembic migration and no deploy-template change, which is what keeps this at L rather than XL.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L (4) to XL (5): touches core shared utilities — the fallback lands in customer_config_service resolve/merge, shared with chatDisclaimer and /v1/applications.

Requirements Clarity bumped from L (4) to XL (5): 'similar to the disclaimer settings' phrasing while the underlying shape differs (three component_ids with a 'value' field vs one id with 'text'), so the analogy does not carry.
Technical Risk bumped from M (3) to L (4): security-sensitive input — bannerLinkRoute is rendered as a route from an unauthenticated public endpoint.
